parts:
Bringing back the discussion to the list

Begin forwarded message:
> From: Jean-Olivier Irisson <iri...@normalesup.org>
> Subject: Re: ggplot2 feature request - scale specific eas, i.e. fontsize
> Date: 2012-March-20 09:50:25 GMT+01:00
> To: Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com>
>
> On 2012-Mar-20, at 04:54 , Alex Brown wrote:
>>
>>> In addition, from a user perspective, it complicates the interface to have several names for the same aesthetic (size and pointsize for point, size and textsize for text etc.).
>>
>> I would argue quite strongly that they are NOT the same aesthetic at all, in fact I'd prefer if there was no common name. However, that would break backward compatibility.
>
> I think of them as properties, which have a different aesthetic consequence depending on the object. It' s important to have consistent names to make them discoverable.
>
> In addition, if you go that route, the size if points is actually diameter so that would be a better name. But diameter is probably more difficult to understand for other shapes, so it becomes hard to find a good name for it that isn't size.
>
>>> Furthermore, still from a UX perspective, I always thought that the "true" ggplot syntax is the ggplot + geom one. qplot is just a shorthand, for quick jobs and/or to make users of the base plot somewhat at home. So you can't ask qplot to do everything that ggplot + geom does, otherwise, it would become too complicated and defeat its purpose of being a quick, simple shorthand.
>>
>> I was only using qplot for compactness.
>
> OK
>
>> However, you should note that the stat_ methods, and the layer method accept multiple geoms.
>
> I know but that supposes that the aesthetic mapping is the same for all geoms, which is probably true in many cases. If you want to do something different in each layer, then it seems conceptually fitting to have to specify each layer separately.
>
>>> But again, that's only my point of view and only Hadley can really say what he wants qplot to be.
>>
>> And a valid one. I use ggplot a lot, and I love it, and want to make it easier for new users and maintainers to understand and use it. As part of this I want to file off the sharp edges that have hit me and every new user. The aesthetic issue is only one of them (and probably quite private to me).
>
> That's the best reason to provide feedback and I saw you provided a lot of it, which is good.
>
> For this particular issue, I think the documentation of ggplot is misleading in that it presents qplot quite often and uses several different plot constructions, giving the impression that all constructions are equally powerful. Hadley agreed that the examples should be made more consistent (and I am working on it when I can). The idea is to start the documentation of all functions with the more versatile syntax:
>
> ggplot() + geom_***(mapping=aes(whatever), data=mydata) + geom_***(…
>
> i.e. specify each layer completely and independently from the others. Then, in later examples, we would start to introduce shorthands such as:
> - specify stuff in the ggplot call which gets inherited by all layers
> - save the plot to an object and modify the object
> - use qplot
> etc.
> But these constructions are special cases of the general syntax, faster to write but less powerful. The verbosity of the general syntax makes it completely clear.
>
> Jean-Olivier Irisson
